skip_reason: Not a sales call. Inbound scope-change request on an already-booked move (packing 9/5, move 9/7, 4 movers / 2 trucks, booked previously by Garrison). The entire call is existing-move logistics — whether to drop the dedicated packing day, whether to keep the Saturday crew, and a recap of rates already on the profile. No new lead, no quote being built, no booking attempt. Grading it against the 9-section sales scorecard would score sections the call type never had a chance to cover.
top_strength: Therese pulled the profile fast, read Garrison's existing note back accurately, and used it to give the customer a clean recommendation instead of just processing a change request: keep the schedule as-is, work the full Saturday, and 'it's easier to remove you from the schedule once we get everything done, rather than to like add things back on.' She also reassured on billing — 'you'll only be charged for the time our movers actually work' — which resolved the customer's real worry (crew showing up expecting to pack all day) without giving away margin. Customer closed with 'it's been super helpful.'
coaching_note: Not scored, but two pricing accuracy issues on this call are worth correcting directly with Therese. First, she told the customer Saturday is the cheaper day — 'Saturday is actually our standard great day so, it's actually cheaper' — while quoting Saturday at $103/hr per mover ($412/hr for four) against Monday the 7th at $96/hr per mover ($384/hr for four). The rates she gave contradict the claim she made about them; the customer walked away repeating '384 on Monday,' so he heard it correctly, but the framing was wrong and could surface as a dispute. Second, her all-in Saturday figure does not reconcile: she quoted $3,564 for seven hours with four movers and two trucks, but 7 x $412 is $2,884, and even adding the $140 round-trip travel fee only reaches $3,024 — roughly $540 unaccounted for and never explained. She should either walk the customer through the line items or not give a total she cannot break down. Third, this was a verbal scope change with a verbal 'no change, just no expectation to pack all day' outcome and no confirmation email offered — that expectation needs to land in EMMA and in writing so the Saturday crew and the customer are working from the same plan.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently courteous and patient with a fair amount of 'yes ma'am' warmth, but the explanations rambled and doubled back ('let me see here... check here... okay see here'), and she never acknowledged the customer's underlying concern in words — the reassurance came out as process detail rather than empathy.
